info.sub_ename: CURRENT TRENDS AND TECHNOLOGIES IN ARCHITECTURE

description.sub_ename: CURRENT TRENDS AND TECHNOLOGIES IN ARCHITECTURE
description.describe_ch:
本課程探討塑造當代建築實踐和討論的重要趨勢和技術。學生將研究新興方法（如電腦工作流程）如何重新定義建築設計過程。主題包括建築信息建模 (BIM) 的進展、可持續和再生設計技術，以及虛擬和增強實境 (VR/AR) 在概念化和展示中的作用。
通過授課和案例研究，學生將深入了解這些技術的變革潛力。重點將放在對工具及其對展現性、物質性和宜居性的影響進行批判性參與。到課程結束時，學生將能夠在快速發展的建築技術環境中運用和創新，將當代建築與技術趨勢審慎有效地整合到他們的專業實踐中。
description.describe_eh:
This course explores the important trends and technologies shaping contemporary architectural practice and discourse. Students will examine how emerging methodologies, such as computational workflows are redefining the architectural design process. Topics include advancements in Building Information Modeling (BIM), sustainable and regenerative design technologies, and the role of Virtual and Augmented Reality (VR/AR) are used in the conceptualization and presentation.
Through lectures and case studies, students will gain insights into the transformative potential of these technologies. Emphasis will be placed on critical engagement with tools and their implications for representation, materiality, and habitability. By the end of the course, students will be equipped to navigate and innovate within the rapidly evolving technological landscape of architecture, preparing them to integrate contemporary trends thoughtfully and effectively into their professional practice.

weeklyScds.tpd_ass_en: Introduction: taking notes as a practice of engagement (EMI)

weeklyScds.tpd_reading:
Teacher 1: Preston Hite on the The 21st-Century Master Builder: Reemergence and Reformation of an Ideal. 
The Collaborative Master Builder: How Computing Supports Collaboration 3D Versus Embedded Intelligence and Creativity Versus Pragmatism Object-oriented Modeling and Parameters for Geometry, Location, and Spatial Relationships
weeklyScds.tpd_ass_en: Lecture and sharing: students present about movies that have directly and indirectly inspired they view on architecture.

weeklyScds.tpd_reading: Understanding Complex Challenges: the owners’ requirements, the parameter-driven conceptual design and model checking: regulations and coordination
weeklyScds.tpd_reading_en: Nicolas Marechal: Architecture as phenomenological experience centered on sustainability. The use of virtual reality as an art of consequence.
weeklyScds.tpd_ass_en: Lecture. Discussion on the consequences of architecture, specifically on sustainability and how it can be changed.

weeklyScds.tpd_reading:
Collaborative Design Processes: How the parts of a building relate to the design process
Emerging Delivery Methods and Lean Thinking and Pull Planning
weeklyScds.tpd_reading_en: Wei Chieh Kung: the guest teacher has studied at the Royal College of Art (UK) and will be sharing his experience after studying an MA, practicing abroad and coming back to Taiwan. His topic will demonstrate his experience: Tree-Timber-Structure: Intimacy between Openness and Geometry.

weeklyScds.tpd_reading:
Making Complex Ideas Buildable: Constructability Analysis, Model-driven Cost Analysis
and Model-guided Construction Planning and Scheduling
weeklyScds.tpd_reading_en: Zhang Ya-Zhu (張雅筑): the guest teacher has studied at the Royal College of Art (UK) and will be sharing her experience on a project called the Blue House which she exhibited at the Taipei Fine Arts Museum. The theme is  architecture as curation.

weeklyScds.tpd_reading: Teacher 2: Shengfang Chou on the Architectural Cultural Narratives and Reimagining Cross-Cultural Identity Through Design.
weeklyScds.tpd_reading_en: Wendy Tao is a malaysian architect who studied at FCU then pass her license in the UK. She will be having 4 classes on the topic of regenerative design. First class is: Why Regenerative Design Matters?

weeklyScds.tpd_reading: Building a Museum: From World Expos to the Legacy of the V&A
weeklyScds.tpd_reading_en: Wendy Tao is a malaysian architect who studied at FCU then pass her license in the UK. She will be having 4 classes on the topic of regenerative design. Second class is: Ancestral Wisdom as the Foundation.

weeklyScds.tpd_reading: Wearable Architecture: The Body as a Design Museum
weeklyScds.tpd_reading_en: Wendy Tao is a malaysian architect who studied at FCU then pass her license in the UK. She will be having 4 classes on the topic of regenerative design. Third class is: Global Case Studies

weeklyScds.tpd_ass_en: No course. For each class, students will be required to take notes, not just what has been said but the question and image they have inspired. Students will be required to upload their notes on iLearn.

weeklyScds.tpd_reading: Curating the Future: Public Art, High-Tech Narratives, and Cultural Sustainability
weeklyScds.tpd_reading_en: Wendy Tao is a malaysian architect who studied at FCU then pass her license in the UK. She will be having 4 classes on the topic of regenerative design. Fourth class is: Unlocking the Potential of Regenerative Design.

weeklyScds.tpd_reading: Teacher 3: Nicolas Marechal: The different roles of virtual reality (VR) in architecture. Virtual reality as a means of representation, participation and performativity.
weeklyScds.tpd_reading_en: Zhang Ya-Zhu (張雅筑): the guest teacher has studied at the Royal College of Art (UK). In her second lecture, she will be talking about her recent return to Chinese cultural traditions and her interpretation toward architecture: Chinese calligraphy and architecture. Void and substance. Tangible and intangible.

weeklyScds.tpd_reading: From Cinema and Post-occupancy to the Virtual Reality and Performativity as methods for re-imagining architecture as an art of consequences.
weeklyScds.tpd_reading_en: Rafael Kim's professional background includes research experience in protein chemistry at Roche Pharmaceuticals, academic roles at Imperial College London and TU Delft, and teaching positions at institutions such as the Royal College of Art. He is the founder of Founder of Biodesign Academy (https://www.biodesign.academy) and will be talking about Sustainable materials.

weeklyScds.tpd_reading: Controversy and Cosmopolitical: situating architecture as socio-material, between the people that builds and the idea that gets built.
weeklyScds.tpd_reading_en: In his second presentation, Raphael Kim will be talking about AI-driven form making

weeklyScds.tpd_reading: Teacher 4: Wendy Teo Boon Ting:  Why Regenerative Design Matters - Explore the pressing need for regenerative practices in design. This session introduces the key principles of regenerative design and highlights its role in addressing global ecological and societal challenges.
weeklyScds.tpd_reading_en: Nicolas Marechal will be presenting a talk on the role of improvisation in architecture. He will be accompanied by Colin Priest, a professor of architecture at the University of the Arts London (UK).

weeklyScds.tpd_reading: Ancestral Wisdom as the Foundation - Delve into the rich legacy of ancestral wisdom and its influence on regenerative design. Learn how traditional practices and cultural knowledge inform sustainable and holistic approaches today.
weeklyScds.tpd_reading_en: Takako Hasegawa will be presenting her research on the relation between dance and architecture at the Architecture Association (AA) (1 out of 2)

weeklyScds.tpd_reading: Global Case Studies - Examine real-world applications of regenerative design across different regions. From architectural innovations to community-led projects, discover inspiring examples and their transformative impacts.
weeklyScds.tpd_reading_en: Takako Hasegawa will be presenting her research on the relation between dance and architecture at the Architecture Association (AA) (2 out of 2)
Nicolas Marechal will concluding the talks, synthesising the main ideas throughout and giving some tips for the final upload.
